analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is documentation. At head lines 99-101 it says each provider test shard is routed through its own CI lane `test-provider-K`, and links to the CI runner routing guide. At head lines 1368-1374 it says the route test now pins each routed job's lanes, one per provider shard, matching the job's matrix. The surrounding text still says release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners and that no check contacts the real plane. No code, workflow, secret handling or runtime behavior changes in this PR. I found no security-relevant regression against the provider threat model (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041 cache or the App Attest assets). The docs make no new claim about attestation, cache storage, key custody, authorization or receipts. The routing logic itself is outside the supplied evidence: the actual `scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and build.md#ci-runner-routing were not provided. I could not verify that the described per-shard lanes match the real workflow, or that the read-only permissions and fallback hold. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not a finding. Release signing lanes are described as unchanged and kept on literal Blacksmith runners. A follow-up pass on the CI workflow diff, if one exists in the PR, should check that the lane labels and matrix cannot let untrusted fork PRs obtain privileged runners.
